name: IL-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: Donna Miller's large fundraising and outside-spending edge
Republican nominee with no reported fundraising
Open seat after Robin Kelly's retirement, but seat held by Democrats
model.rationale: The district's D+18 lean and a favorable national environment point to a wide Democratic margin, and prediction markets price the Democratic nominee near 96%. Miller has raised $2.7 million with over $4.4 million in outside support, while Noack shows no reported fundraising, leaving no evidence of a competitive race.
model.watch: Any late polling or unexpected outside spending surge for the Republican nominee would be the first sign the race is tightening.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Robin Kelly (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
This south Chicago-area seat has been held by Democrats for years and carries an 18-point Democratic partisan lean. Robin Kelly is retiring to run for Senate, but the open seat remains firmly in Democratic territory. Donna Miller enters the general election with a substantial financial advantage, having raised $2.7 million and benefited from more than $4.4 million in outside support, while Republican Michael Noack reports no fundraising activity.

No public general-election polling exists for this race, and no expert raters have flagged it as competitive. Prediction markets price the Democratic nominee at roughly 96 percent to win. With the fundamentals, money, and market pricing all aligned, the race is rated Safe Democratic, with the main uncertainty being the absence of direct polling in the district.
